chapter: Return to Chicago: the Blue Note and Rupneck's
title: Eighteen months at Rupneck's
summary: Hodes describes Frank Rupneck's place, the trumpeters, a drummer, and Floyd O'Brien. The boss's Rampart Street Parade request cost a trumpeter his lip.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: So I did the best I could. And I stayed at Rup- neck's 18 months the first time.

That was 5900 North Broadway on Thorndale, I think it was, right around the corner. And tremendous, we packed the joint. And I had Floyd O'Bryan and different trumpet players. I had little Muggsy Davis I had Jimmy Isle for awhile, different people.

No, we didn't have a bass player. I did have a black drummer and I can't think of his name. But he was more like a Mexican, and he'd worked with a band that made what they called race records at that time in Chicago, and they had a New Orleans trumpet player -- I can't think of his name.
That wasn't Booker T. playing drums, Booker T. Washington?
No, no, I can't think of his name. But, anyway, he worked in the post office, this guy. But, again, he used to really overdrink and I had to change that. But we lasted.

That was the job where Floyd O'Bryan sat at the bar and the boss bought us a drink, and the boss must have -- Floyd, 'were losing money. And Floyd looked at him and says, bullshit. Because talk like that was unheard of. That was the same boss that loved "Rampart Street Parade." That was his number. And anytime we bought a drink for the band, play

Frank Rupneck. Well, now, it just happened that in that period I was using two trumpet players. One would come in at 9:00 and play til 12:00, and one would come in at 12:30 and go till 3:00. It was a 9:00 to 3:00 job. Now, Frank bought the band a drink and the new trumpet player has gone up there. He hasn't played yet. We got to play Rampart.
Well, you know what happened to his lip? He just blew the number. And Frank cut us off from the bar, he says, don't give him anymore to drink.
And had nothing. He just walked in cold with a cold lip.
